correctness.rationale: For \(m=2r\), an old-zero peripheral bit adopts one iff \(k_i+c\ge r+1\) and an old-one bit retains one iff \(k_i+c\ge r+1\): hence all members of each clique agree after one step. A monochromatic clique remains so because its \(m-1\) internal neighbors form at least a tie-resistant majority against the hub. For odd n the hub becomes the strict majority of these frozen clique bits at time two, proving \(F^3=F^2\). The explicit \((n+1)/2\) cliques with \(k_i=r+1\), others zero, and initial hub zero witness sharpness for every \(n\ge3,r\ge2\). The initial hub conditions give \(u_m\) and \(v_m\) choices independently per clique, so individual basin weights follow; summing yields \(2^{nm+1}\). The central-binomial Stirling approximation and triangular-array binomial CLT yield \(\Phi(\sqrt{2\lambda/\pi})\); Chebyshev handles \(n/m\) tending to infinity. Two independent direct graph-update checkers replayed all 8192, 524288, and 2097152 states in their reported test cases. This is a mathematical proof for the entire stated domain; enumeration is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical articulation of highly connected modules in opinion dynamics, where local-majority amplification and the exceptional hub create two nested scales. An exact natural invariant, the fibre sizes of each terminal fixed state, has a closed expression, reveals unique extremal fixed configurations, and determines the initial-hub/final-hub correlation. The Gaussian transition when \(n/m\) tends to a constant isolates a nontrivial competition between module size and number that is not available from general period-two or voting-time bounds. This is a structurally motivated all-parameters classification, rather than an arbitrary finite sample or a routine parameter increment.
